title: Appending a logged step to the history
statement: Let $c$ be a configuration of a $k$-work-tape Boolean machine on input $x$, let $h$ be a finite list of history entries, and let $a$ be an action for that machine. Applying the corresponding logged action to the configuration encoding $c$ and $h$ gives the encoding of the configuration obtained by applying $a$ to $c$, with the history extended by one entry consisting of the symbols scanned before the step and the work-head movements prescribed by $a$.
hypotheses_covered: Finite history list $h$ of entries for $k$ work tapes
replaced:
For any configuration $c$ with history $h$ and any action $a$ of the source
machine: applying the logged version of $a$ to the logged configuration of $c$
with history $h$ yields the logged configuration of $a$ applied to $c$, with
history $h$ extended by the single entry recording the overwritten symbols and
head moves of $a$. This includes halting and output-emitting actions.
